note: rows = citation rows of the JSTOR rule parser (rules/part-*, textnotes-rules); a row that refers back (Ibid., short form, author-date) counts for its full citation; citations = rows, pairs = distinct (citing article, cited work); before = data/graph/jstor-cites.csv.gz as built into build/graph/cites.parquet (source jstor, edition rows included); after = before + this crosswalk

denominator.note: a_matched = the earlier matcher found and the export kept a graph work; b_attemptable = parsed with an author and a usable title and not exported (unmatched, matched only ambiguously, or an unresolved short form of 3+ title words); c = archival/primary, Ibid./author-date with nothing to resolve to, fragments (no author or no title), unparsed or commentary, titles too short, newspapers/periodicals, web. Rows that refer back count in the group of their full citation. Book-review items are counted but never matched (they give no citations).

audit.note: hand-judged 2026-11-11 against the note piece and the catalogue record; 250/250 right

supplement_lc_initials_year_before.note: released after the main sample: initials-only LC matches whose cited year is 3+ years before LC; cited years are often the first year of a date range in the title (1917-1942), or the first edition where LC holds a reprint

audit_crossref_meta.target: crossref-meta (Crossref metadata harvest) matches of JSTOR note citations, new pairs only
audit_crossref_meta.action: short_title_container 26/27 (96.3%) < 97%: tightened by holding short-title matches whose cited container names an edited volume (eds., edited by, 2nd ed., dir., edition): 3 forms held, all three the error class of the one wrong row; the other 26 sampled rows of that basis are unaffected
audit_crossref_meta.judged_from: parsed citation fields (author, title, year, container) and the note piece against the Crossref record (title, year, journal, author families, pages)

whole_title_extra.note: whole_title holds 92% of the new pairs: a second random draw of 40 from that basis only (whole-extra/sample.csv); whole_title combined 67/67
